title: Pruning preserves outputs on inputs that miss the subprotocol
statement: Let $s$ and $p$ be deterministic two-party communication protocols over Alice's inputs $X$, Bob's inputs $Y$, and output type $\alpha$, and suppose $s$ is a subprotocol of $p$ (a rooted subtree) whose leaf count is strictly smaller than that of $p$. Form the pruned protocol obtained by deleting the subtree $s$ from $p$. Then for every pair of inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$ that does not reach $s$ — that is, $(x,y)$ fails to be consistent with all of the branching choices along the path from the root of $p$ down to $s$ — the pruned protocol and $p$ produce the same output on $(x,y)$: running the pruned protocol on $x$ and $y$ yields exactly $p$'s output on $x$ and $y$.
hypotheses_covered: s is a subprotocol of p
inputs x in X and y in Y
replaced:
If $s.\mathrm{numLeaves} < p.\mathrm{numLeaves}$ and $(x, y)$ does not reach $s$, then
$(\texttt{prune}\;\texttt{hsp}\;\texttt{hlt}).\texttt{run}\;x\;y = p.\texttt{run}\;x\;y$.
